column2: How do I speed up or slow down a video or a sound in the montage?
column3: Choose the clip on the timeline, 🎯 Item tab → “Speed”: from 0.25 × to 4 × (or the 0.5 × 1 × 1.5 × 2 × buttons). The clip gets longer or shorter on the timeline; “keep the pitch of the voice” avoids the duck voice.

column2: How do I make a photo last as long as I want in the montage?
column3: Choose the photo on the timeline, 🎯 Item tab → “Time on screen”: type the seconds (for example 5, or 12.5), or click 2 s, 3 s, 5 s, 8 s, 10 s, 15 s.

column2: How do I adjust the sound of a single clip, or of the whole montage?
column3: One clip: choose it, 🎯 Item tab → “🔊 Sound of this clip”: clearer voice, less hiss, bass, treble, mono (and volume, fades for a sound). “Apply to all the sounds of the project” copies these settings everywhere. The whole film at once: 🔊 Sound tab (same settings, plus the overall volume and “without sound”).

column2: How do I undo in the montage?
column3: ⌘Z undoes the last change (cut with B, move, adjust…), ⇧⌘Z redoes it; also the ↶ ↷ buttons at the start of the toolbar.

column2: How do I zoom in an editor (retouching, drawing, layout, house, montage…)?
column3: All editors have the same bar at the bottom: on the right “− 100 % ▾ +”. Click the percentage for “Fit to window”, 50 %, 100 % or 200 %. With the keyboard: ⌘ + and ⌘ − (Ctrl on a PC), ⌘ 0 to fit, ⌘ 1 for 100 %; or ⌘ + the mouse wheel. On the left of this bar: where you are (page, layer, slide…); in the middle: help for the chosen tool.

column2: What is 🧲 at the bottom of an editor for?
column3: 🧲 Snap: while dragging, objects stick to others, to the edges, to the guides or to the grid. Click 🧲 to turn it on or off; the tooltip tells you which key to hold down to do without it for one gesture. 📏 next to it shows or hides the rulers and guides (when the editor has them).

column2: Where have the tools and the “Save…” buttons at the bottom of the editors gone?
column3: The tools are in the narrow column on the left (same place in all editors; hover over them for their name and key). The ways of saving (show this version, without showing it, separate copy, keep in media…) are at the top: click ▾ next to “💾 Save”.

column2: How do I arrange a list with the keyboard?
column3: Each line that can be arranged has a grey ⠿ handle on the left: drag it, or go to it with Tab and press Alt + ↑ or Alt + ↓ (⌥ on a Mac). In Appearance, the order is saved straight away (“✓ Saved”, and “↶ Undo” at the bottom left).

column2: Do record transcription and quick retouching have “Undo”?
column3: Yes: ↶ and ↷ at the top (or ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z) undo and redo everything: text, title, areas, image settings, retouches. In a text box, ⌘Z first undoes what you have just typed. The File, Edit, Tools and View menus are also at the top.

column2: Can I have the calculator directly on the dashboard?
column3: Yes: in the left column of the Dashboard, add the “🧮 Calculator” widget with ＋. Type your calculation and press Enter; the last 5 calculations stay below (click to reuse them, ↑ for the last one). “⛶ Open the calculator” opens the big calculator (scientific, graphs).

column2: Where has the events’ 📅 “＋ Add to my calendar” button gone?
column3: It is hidden by default. To show it on the events of records: open My diary → ⚙️ Settings, then tick “Show the 📅 ＋ Add to my calendar button on record events”. The change is kept straight away.

column2: The settings of My diary or of books no longer have a “Save” button: is that normal?
column3: Yes: each change is kept straight away (“✓ Saved” at the top of the window), and “↶ Undo” at the bottom left undoes it. “↺ Reset to default” puts back the original settings, without a question. “Close” closes the window.

column2: How do I set my own shortcuts in the montage, sound, retouching or layout?
column3: Settings → “Montage, retouching, layout and sound” → ⌨️ Your own shortcuts (or Settings → Keyboard shortcuts, at the bottom). Choose the tool at the top, then “Choose” next to the command and press the key. A key already taken by the system (macOS, Windows, Linux) or by the application menu is refused; if it is already used in the tool, you are warned and your shortcut takes priority. Without ⌘ / Ctrl, it only works outside text boxes. ✕ removes a shortcut.

column2: Layout: how do I apply, remove or replace a master on a page?
column3: Pages panel → Masters: the “Page N” list changes the master of the current page (or “No master” to remove it). “Several pages…” (also in the Page menu) does it on all pages, a range, the left or right pages, or replaces one master by another wherever it is. When you delete a master, you choose the one its pages take. ⌘Z undoes.

column2: How do I make a note built the same way again (same order of blocks)?
column3: In the note: “⧉ Duplicate”, then “▦ The same order of blocks” (a new note with the same blocks, titles, widths and colours, but empty) or “⭐ Make it a template” (you can also keep the texts, dates, links and people; images do not go into a template). Your templates appear in “New note”, under “Start from”, in “⭐ My templates” (✎ to edit it, 🗑 to delete it), and at the bottom of “My notes”. Deleting a template does not change the notes already created with it.

column2: How do I come back later to a sound I am working on?
column3: In “Edit the sound”: “💾 Save the project” (at the bottom left, or ⌘S; ⇧⌘S for a copy under another name) keeps the sound in progress, without loss, separately from Media. To come back to it: “📂 Projects…” in “Edit the sound”, Lists → 🎧 Audio → “📂 Sound projects”, or Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → 🎧 Sound. To start one: Lists → 🎧 Audio → “＋ New sound project” (a sound from the database or from the computer). When the sound is finished, “💾 Save…” makes a version, a copy or a new sound of it.

column2: What is “⚡ Quick sound” and how do I get it?
column3: A window with big buttons to clean up a sound in two minutes: 🧹 hiss, ✨ clicks and crackles, 〰️ mains hum (found by itself, 50 or 60 Hz), 🗣️ clearer voice, 📏 even volume, ✂️ start and end trimmed (black handles on the waveform), ⏩ silences shortened; strength Gentle / Medium / Strong; “✨ Clean everything at once”. By default, “✂️ Edit” on a sound keeps the previous editor (“🎧 Edit the sound”); for the new one: Settings → Montage, retouching, layout and sound → 🎧 Sound → “⚡ Quick sound: the design” → “New ⚡ Quick sound” (kept by itself). Three choices: “As before” (the original editor, each tool with its name), “As before, tidied” (the same, tools in a column on the left and bottom bar shared with the other editors) and “New ⚡ Quick sound”. Nothing is damaged until you have saved: the original stays in the versions.

column2: How do I compare the sound before and after cleaning?
column3: In ⚡ Quick sound: 👂 Before / ✨ After, at the same place in playback (the sound continues, you only switch), or hold down the A key to hear the before. In 🎚️ Sound studio, holding A plays the sound without the rack’s effects.

column2: What is the “🎚️ Sound studio”?
column3: The full version, in the style of Adobe Audition: waveform with selection, overview of the whole sound, zoom, 🚩 markers and named coloured regions, VU meters, clickable history ↶ ↷; an effects rack you can adjust at any time (graphic and parametric equalisers, compressor, limiter, noise reduction with a noise print, De-clicker, De-hum, De-esser, reverb, speed and pitch, normalise, even volume, fades with 4 curves): ⠿ to arrange, 👁 to switch off, × to remove, “Only on the selection”; the spectrum and its repair brush; Multitrack; transcription. You get there with “🎚️ Sound studio” in Quick sound (or the previous editor), or Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → 🎧 Sound → “＋ New sound project”.

column2: I switch from Quick sound to Sound studio: do I lose my settings?
column3: No, the work follows: each button switched on becomes an effect in the rack, already set; the trimmed start and end become cuts of the waveform (in the history). When you go back (“⚡ Quick sound”), what Quick sound can show comes back as buttons; the rest stays applied and a badge says so (“2 Studio settings remain applied”). The last choice is remembered: “✂️ Edit” reopens the same one.

column2: How do I remove a cough or a ringtone in the middle of a sentence?
column3: In 🎚️ Sound studio, “Spectrum” switch on: the cough shows as a bright patch. Take 🖌 (brush, B key) or ➰ (lasso), paint over the patch, then “🩹 Repair”: it is replaced by what surrounds it, without touching the words around it. Each repair is in the rack and the history (it can be removed).

column2: How do I link a passage of a sound to a person? Where can it be heard afterwards?
column3: In 🎚️ Sound studio: select the passage, “＋ New region” (or M), give it a name; then in “🔗 Link this passage” choose the person (the usual picker, with a role: speaks, sings, tells…) and, if you like, an event. Right-click a region: “🔗 Link to a person…”. On the person’s record, the “🎧 Heard here” block lists their passages: ▶ plays just that passage.

column2: How do I transcribe what is said in a sound?
column3: In 🎚️ Sound studio, Window → 📝 Transcription: listen, “⏱ Insert the time” (⌘T) and type what is said, with who is speaking. “🐢 Play at 75 %” slows it down, “Pause while I type” stops playback while you type. Clicking a time plays that passage. The text is searchable, and can be exported as .txt, .srt or .vtt (⤓ Export → 📝 Text and markers). Automatic transcription (an engine on the computer) will come later.

column2: How do I make a “family podcast” with music under the voice?
column3: 🎚️ Sound studio → “🎛️ Multitrack” tab: Voice, Music, Sound effects tracks (and others), with volume, pan, M (mute), S (solo), ● (arm to record from the microphone). “＋ Add a sound…” places a sound on a track (or drag it from “Files”). Turn on “🔉 Lower the music under the voice”: the music goes down by itself when the voice speaks. The yellow line is the volume curve: drag its ◆ points, double-click to add one, right-click to remove one.

column2: How do I rescue an old cassette step by step?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → 🎧 Sound → “🧭 Rescue an old cassette”: choose the sound, then follow the steps (listen, hiss, hum and clicks, voice, start and end, save). Each step switches on the right button; compare with 👂 Before / ✨ After.

column2: How do I record a sound from the microphone?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → 🎧 Sound → “🎙️ Record from the microphone”: ● Start, then ⏹; the sound goes into the media and opens in 🎚️ Sound studio. In the Studio, ● (under the waveform) records at the orange marker; in Multitrack, on the armed track ●.

column2: Which formats can I export a sound in?
column3: ⤓ Export: MP3 (plays everywhere), M4A (iPhone, iTunes — only if your browser can do it), WAV, FLAC (lossless), Ogg Opus (the lightest), AIFF (GarageBand, Logic), 📝 Text and markers (.txt, .srt, .vtt, .cue). You choose the quality, “What” (everything, the selection, each region in a file, each track in a file), the channels and the sample rate; “Write the regions and people into the file” puts the title and chapters into the MP3 or FLAC.
